title: Anesthesiologist Services
description:
10 hours per week
Tuesdays and Thursday

Overview:

The Anesthesiologist provides comprehensive anesthesia care to patients undergoing medical, dental, or psychiatric procedures within a state-operated psychiatric center. This role involves ensuring the safe administration of anesthesia and sedation, evaluating patients' medical conditions prior to procedures, and collaborating with a multidisciplinary team to support the overall health and safety of individuals with complex psychiatric and medical needs.

Description of Services:

The Anesthesiologist will be responsible for performing professional medical work in the field of anesthesiology, including but not limited to:

  • Pre-Procedure Assessment:

    • Conduct pre-anesthetic evaluations to determine patients' physical status, psychiatric history, and any factors that may influence anesthesia management.

    • Review medical charts, laboratory results, and consult with psychiatrists, physicians, and nurses to establish safe anesthesia plans.

  • Administration of Anesthesia:

    • Administer general, regional, or local anesthesia, and sedation for a variety of procedures including electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), dental procedures, or emergency medical interventions.

    • Monitor patients continuously during anesthesia to ensure stability of vital signs and responsiveness to treatment.

  • Post-Anesthesia Care:

    • Provide post-anesthesia monitoring and management until patients safely recover from sedation or anesthesia.

    • Address any complications or adverse reactions promptly and document all findings in the medical record.

  • Collaboration & Consultation:

    • Work closely with psychiatrists, nurses, and other clinical staff to ensure safe and coordinated patient care.

    • Provide guidance regarding anesthesia risk management and contribute to patient treatment planning when necessary.

  • Compliance and Documentation:

    • Maintain accurate, timely, and complete anesthesia records in accordance with facility policies and state and federal regulations.

    • Follow all safety protocols and standards of practice established by the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) and relevant governing bodies.

Qualifications:

  • Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathy (DO) degree.

  • Completion of an accredited anesthesiology residency program.

  • Current license to practice medicine in the State of New York (or applicable state).

  • Board Certification or Board Eligibility in Anesthesiology.

  • Current certification in Basic and Advanced Cardiac Life Support (BLS, ACLS).

  • Experience in hospital or psychiatric settings preferred, particularly with ECT or procedures involving behavioral health populations.

Schedule and Work Setting:

  • Services may be required on a part-time, per diem, or scheduled basis, depending on facility needs.

  • Most anesthesia services will be provided in the medical suite, ECT suite, or designated treatment areas within the psychiatric center.

  • The role may require collaboration with other departments to support patients with co-occurring medical and psychiatric conditions.

Division of Adult Care Facilities and Assisted Living Surveillance (2 positions )
Duties Description

T he Division of Adult Care Facilities and Assisted Living Surveillance is responsible for the licensure and surveillance of 548 Adult Care Facilities (ACF) in accordance with State laws, regulations and codes, as well as the investigation of ACF complaints.

This position is with the Central NY Regional Office, based out of Syracuse, NY. The nurse surveyor will be part of an interdisciplinary team of professionals whose primary responsibility will be to conduct onsite inspections of Adult Care Facilities (ACF) located within a 14-county radius to determine operational compliance with applicable laws and regulations. Prior to completing onsite survey work, the nurse surveyor will work with the team, review all pertinent facility information and survey history, and participates in pre-survey meetings when appropriate, in order to develop a plan to effectively measure facility compliance.

Minimum Qualifications: Candidate must be a Registered Professional Nurse, licensed and currently registered to practice nursing in New York State. In addition, the Candidate must have excellent telephone, listening and written communication skills, working knowledge of all Microsoft Office products and experience with complex data entry systems.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills; proficiency in working with MS Office products and exceptional organizational skills are required.

Preferred Qualifications: The ideal Candidate will have professional skills including nursing surveillance, clinical skills, excellent writing and editing skills, and proficiency navigating computer applications used for surveillance or utilization review, SharePoint, and the Electronic Plan of Correction system, and has the ability to expeditiously and effectively interpret laws and regulations governing adult care and assisted living facilities in New York State.

Responsibilities : Candidate will conduct onsite inspections of Adult Care Facilities (ACF) located within a 14-county radius in Central NY to determine operational compliance with applicable laws and regulation.

Additional responsibilities will include, but are not limited to: review complaint intakes, investigation of complaints, review of facility generated incident reports, report development using applicable computer programs, review of Plan s of Correction, review of applications for new licensed and certified programs, review of facility Policies and Procedures, preparation of general correspondence, participation in meetings and on committees, and participation in Enforcement Action against ACFs including testifying at hearings.
